background: National Australia Bank is one of Australia's big four banks and the largest business lender in the country, funded by Australian and New Zealand deposits and wholesale markets, with BNZ as its New Zealand subsidiary.
synthesis: Ratings are AA- from Fitch after the upgrade on 26 May 2024, AA- from S&P and Aa2 from Moody's, all stable. Against Australian peers capital is mixed: CET1 of 11.9% is a shade under the 12.0% median, while leverage of 4.8% is in the top quarter, at the median. Liquidity is strong, with LCR of 134% and NSFR of 115% both in the top quarter, each at the median of a tightly bunched group. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods. Nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days. A typical Australian major on the figures with the same high ratings as its peers.
